transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-14
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Redwood (Aisha Patel, Marcus Lee); Opal Networks (Lina, Diego, Anil, Priya, Evan)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in focused on Opal's planned 40% capacity uplift, requirement for an EU-FR sovereignty zone, and evaluating a private on-prem pilot vs Dedicated reserved capacity. Security/compliance gating items surfaced; clear next steps and pilot timeline agreed.

Topics: capacity uplift, region sovereignty (EU-FR), private/on-prem pilot, contract extension terms, SOC2/KMS/KMS HSM integration, benchmarks and latency SLOs.

[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump in.
[00:12] Lina Sorensen: Hi, Lina here. Thanks Aisha.
[00:14] Diego Marques: Diego, hey.
[00:16] Marcus Lee: Marcus from Redwood SE.
[00:18] Anil Rao: Anil on infra.
[00:20] Priya Venkat: Priya, legal/compliance.
[00:21] Evan Park: Evan, ML.
[00:23] Aisha Patel: Great. Goal today: align on Opal's capacity needs for H2 ramp, review sovereignty ask for France region, and talk pilot approach so you can decide on the contract extension.

[01:05] Diego: Yeah so to be blunt, our surge last quarter means we need more predictable throughput. We're looking at roughly a 40% uplift over current committed GPUs, and we need to make sure any deployment in EU meets our data residency and KMS needs.

[01:35] Marcus: Understood. When you say 40% uplift—are you talking reserved capacity (Dedicated) or we'd be evaluating a private on-prem package?

[01:47] Diego: Preferably Dedicated, but security wants an option for a private on-prem pilot in a single FR cluster first. They want to see audit logs and KMS integration before we extend the contract.

[02:10] Priya: Yes, from a compliance perspective we'll need RBAC, SSO via SAML, encryption at rest with our HSM-backed KMS, and a retention policy that is configurable per tenant.

[02:28] Aisha: That's all supported in our Private deployment and most things for Dedicated with KMS integrations. We'll map what differs. Marcus, can you outline the technical tradeoffs?

[02:40] Marcus: Sure. Quick note, transcription might mess up some terms—sorry if I stumble. For Dedicated: pro is predictable throughput and simpler ops; con is data still flows through our hosted control plane unless you choose Redwood Private which gives you customer-managed control plane and full network isolation. The private on-prem pilot gives you HSM/KMS to keep keys local but increases ops burden and lead time.

[03:20] Evan: Latency is a big deal for our user flows. Our 95th percentile needs to be under 220ms for short shot prompts. Any private deployment on bare-metal in FR — will that meet latency vs your hosted EU nodes?

[03:38] Marcus: It depends on hardware and kernel optimizations. Our EU hosted clusters are typically optimized for 70–120ms p95 on the model families you've run. Private on-prem could match or beat that if you provision similar GPUs, and we can ship the same runtime, but you'll need NVLink topology and kernel compatibility. We'll list minimum specs in the runbook.

[04:10] Lina: And what about cost? We need a clear delta hosted vs dedicated vs private.

[04:18] Aisha: We'll share pricing tiers. For a 40% uplift reserved commit, there are stepped discounts; private pilot has a separate onboarding fee + infra estimates. I'll send scenarios after this call.

[04:40] Diego: Also, fallback during capacity spikes — we need graceful degradation. If the private cluster hits limits, can we failover to hosted in another region?

[04:52] Marcus: Yes, smart routing supports failover to compatible model variants in other regions. You can set routing policy: prefer FR private, fallback to EU-hosted or a lower-cost variant. There are tradeoffs in latency and token cost.

[05:20] Anil: For the private pilot, network setup will be our thing. We need a VPC peering diagram and details on which ports and routes Redwood needs. Also audit logs forwarding to our SIEM.

[05:40] Aisha: We'll attach a tech diagram and a checklist. Marcus, note to add SIEM log endpoints and port list to action items.

[06:00] Marcus: Noted.

[06:12] Priya: A point on the contract — we want a 12-month extension but with a clause that allows capacity rebalancing after Q1 if usage materially exceeds forecasts. Is that something Redwood can accommodate?

[06:30] Aisha: We can include a review clause and a capacity flex window. We usually bake in 30-day rebalancing notices for Dedicated; for Private there is more lead time. We'll put options in the term sheet.

[07:00] Evan: Benchmarks — can we run a quick end-to-end latency and throughput test during the pilot? We'll need token-level traces and cost metrics per 1M tokens.

[07:15] Marcus: Absolutely. Pilot runbook will include a benchmark harness (open-source style) and we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost-per-token. We'll also provide a sample prompt set so results are comparable.

[07:45] Diego: On residency: our legal wants to ensure keys never leave FR. KMS provider is currently Thales, HSM-backed. Can Redwood integrate with an external HSM?

[08:02] Marcus: We support bring-your-own-KMS with external HSMs in Private; for Dedicated we have partner KMS integrations but keys may be under Redwood-managed HSM depending on the flow. We'll call out differences in the doc.

[08:30] Priya: Also, SOC2 reports and penetration test results — we'll need the latest and the process for audit logs.

[08:42] Aisha: We'll attach SOC2 Type II and our pentest summary. For audits, we can provide scoped logs and support.

[09:05] Lina: Timeline question — if we sign the extension this month, how soon can private pilot hardware be staged?

[09:16] Marcus: Typical lead for private on-prem pilot is 4–6 weeks for procurement + integration. For a Dedicated capacity bump alone, we can stage within 14–21 days depending on region capacity.

[09:40] Diego: Hmm we were hoping to run pilot in late June. That might be aggressive.

[09:46] Aisha: For June 22 kickoff it's tight but possible if Opal can pre-approve the runbook and commit to procurement resources this week. We'll treat it as a best-effort schedule.

[10:05] Evan: On models — we're standardizing on an M-family open model. Are there quantization profiles Redwood recommends for cost reduction without harming quality?

[10:20] Marcus: Yes, Optimize will suggest q4/8-bit quantization options and recommended kernels. We'll include model-specific tradeoffs for your prompt distribution.

[10:45] Diego: One more operational ask — token-level billing detail at the route level for the next quarter.

[10:52] Aisha: We can expose per-route cost in Console; we'll provide a sample CSV export.

[11:20] Priya: Legal — indemnity language around data breaches, and a carveout for data processed during the pilot. We'll need to loop in our legal counsel after you send the terms.

[11:35] Aisha: Understood. We'll include a pilot-specific data-handling appendix.

[12:00] (brief cross-talk)
[12:05] Marcus: Action items recap: runbook, pricing scenarios, KMS options, SIEM endpoints, pilot schedule.

[12:25] Diego: Could you also include a comparison vs Google Vertex and Anthropic? We're evaluating those too.

[12:34] Aisha: We'll add a short competitive note but won't over-polish — high level differences in pricing predictability and private deployment options.

[13:00] Evan: For the benchmark prompt set, we'll send a trimmed set of 200 representative prompts. Expect that today.

[13:10] Diego: We'll aim to have the traffic spreadsheet to you by 2027-06-17.

[13:22] Aisha: Great. Any other concerns?
[13:28] Lina: One small thing — our infra team cares about cold-start for KV caches, how Redwood handles cache priming for multi-tenant workloads.

[13:40] Marcus: We do prefix/KV caching strategies; for private pilots we'll recommend a cache warming strategy and autoscaling thresholds to avoid cold penalties. I'll add that to the runbook.

[14:05] Priya: Data sovereignty confirmation: anything that leaves FR for hosted support must be encrypted and subject to our legal review.

[14:15] Aisha: Noted. We'll make that explicit.

[14:30] Diego: Ok, so next steps and timeline again?

[14:35] Aisha: Short list: Redwood sends pricing + term options and the pilot runbook by 2027-06-18. Opal provides traffic spreadsheet by 2027-06-17 and compliance answers by 2027-06-21. Tentative pilot kickoff week of 2027-06-22 if procurement clears.

[15:00] (someone laughs)
[15:05] Marcus: I'll also add the port list and SIEM webhook details.

[15:12] Diego: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[15:18] Aisha: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with attachments.

[51:10] (call ends, recording stops)

Notes on transcript accuracy: automated transcript with occasional mis-hears (e.g., HSM provider may appear as "the H S M Thales" or "Thales-H S M"); speaker labels verified where possible but may have a few speaker attribution errors.

References/Artifacts mentioned:
- Pilot runbook (to be shared by Redwood)
- Pricing scenarios spreadsheet (to be shared by Aisha)
- SOC2 Type II and pentest summary (attachments)
- Traffic/token spreadsheet (from Opal)

Recap of decisions during call:
- Opal to pursue a 40% committed uplift; Redwood to produce pricing for Dedicated and Private pilot scenarios
- Private on-prem pilot in EU-FR favored for KMS/HSM requirements; target pilot kickoff week of 2027-06-22 (contingent on procurement)
- Benchmarking harness agreed; both teams to exchange prompt set and traffic data

End of transcript.
